title: Senator Rick Scott announces bill to support older Americans in the workforce at Senate hearing - Duval Times
text:
Senator Rick Scott, chair of the Senate Special Committee on Aging, announced the Senior Citizens’ Freedom to Work Act during a committee hearing titled “Experience Matters: Older Americans and the Workforce” on March 25. The proposed legislation aims to remove barriers and increase flexibility for older Americans who wish to remain active in the workforce.
The announcement is significant as it addresses financial challenges faced by seniors who want to continue working. The bill would repeal the Social Security Retirement Earnings Test, allowing seniors to earn income without reductions in their Social Security benefits. Senator Tommy Tuberville is a co-sponsor of the bill in the Senate, while Representative Greg Murphy leads companion legislation in the House.
Scott was joined at the hearing by witnesses Rachel Greszler, senior fellow at Advancing American Freedom; Johnny C. Taylor Jr., president and CEO of SHRM; and Jason J. Fichtner, Ph.D., senior fellow at the National Academy of Social Insurance. These experts discussed contributions made by older adults to America’s workforce and economy, as well as obstacles they face when seeking employment opportunities.
The committee’s work includes providing resources such as a fraud hotline aimed at protecting older Americans from scams and financial exploitation according to its official website. The committee also operates offices in both Dirksen (majority) and Hart (minority) Senate Office Buildings according to its official website.
The committee examines issues impacting seniors including Social Security, Medicare, long-term care, retirement security, holds hearings and releases reports according to its official website. Scott serves as chair with Kirsten Gillibrand as ranking member according to its official website. Its oversight covers aging-related federal programs nationwide according to its official website, including regular review of Medicare, Social Security and elder abuse prevention efforts through hearings and policy recommendations according to its official website.
The broader impact of this legislation could be an increase in workforce participation among seniors while supporting their financial independence.
